# Coverage map staleness (auto-generated by `python -m utr coverage-eval`)

A coverage map built from the sounding 12 h earlier is compared with the map built from the sounding itself, both with the reference solver, over cells beyond 5 km and 5-300 m high where either map is above -40 dB.
- Rows: {'train': 20764, 'validation': 2696, 'test': 9565} (train to 2020, validation 2021 fixes the cut-offs, test 2022 onward)
- Error of using the 12-hour-old map, test period: mean 3.4 dB, median 2.7 dB, 90th percentile 7.1 dB. By year: 2022: 3.7, 2023: 3.2, 2024: 3.3, 2025: 3.2
- A gradient-boosting model predicts how much the map will have moved, from the same inputs as the hourly now-cast. Rank correlation with the real change: 0.56. Mean absolute error 1.54 dB, against 1.96 dB for always guessing the typical value.

## Green / yellow / red for a coverage map

| Light | Share of hours | Mean change in coverage map | 90th percentile |
|---|---|---|---|
| green | 52% | 2.2 dB | 4.4 dB |
| yellow | 34% | 4.0 dB | 7.5 dB |
| red | 14% | 6.2 dB | 8.9 dB |

Red means the map has probably moved enough that the full simulation should be rerun.
